observation_summary: The code in DateTimeFormatter.java calculates 'defaultYear' using 'instantLocal' (instantMillis + offset). When the offset is negative (e.g., New York), this can shift the time into the previous year, causing the parser to use the wrong year for leap year validation, resulting in an IllegalFieldValueException when parsing '2 29'.
hypothesis: The bug is caused by an incorrect calculation of the 'defaultYear' in DateTimeFormatter.parseInto. The code currently calculates the year based on 'instantLocal' (which includes the timezone offset), but it should be based on the UTC instant to ensure consistency across different timezones when parsing partial dates like '2 29'.
prediction: The fix will involve changing the calculation of 'defaultYear' to use 'instantMillis' (the UTC time) instead of 'instantLocal' (the local time), ensuring the year is correctly identified regardless of the timezone offset.
